input: This passage presents the results of a performance assessment carried out on a shell-and-tube heat exchanger that heats cooling water as part of a refinery preheat train. The exchanger was found to have a duty of 1287 kW under the conditions examined. On the hot side, the stream enters the exchanger at 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C, while on the cold side, the cooling water enters at 35 °C and leaves at 60 °C. Taking these terminal temperatures into account, the log-mean temperature difference for the unit works out to 82.3 K. The exchanger has an installed area of 52.8 m2, and when the duty, the area, and the log-mean temperature difference are combined, the overall heat transfer coefficient comes out to 296 W m-2 K-1, which reflects the performance of the unit as assessed. It is important to note that the fouling of the exchanger was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and that no cleaning cycle has been completed as yet. Because of this, the picture of how fouling develops over the 90 days and beyond remains incomplete at this stage, and the coefficient reported here should be understood in that context when it is used for further comparison or design purposes. The temperatures recorded during the run were nevertheless consistent, and the exchanger continued to deliver its heating duty to the preheat train throughout the period that was covered by the assessment, with the cooling water leaving the unit at its intended outlet condition on the cold side.
target: A shell-and-tube exchanger in a refinery preheat train heats cooling water at a duty of 1287 kW. The hot stream enters at 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C; the cooling water enters at 35 °C and leaves at 60 °C. The log-mean temperature difference across the unit is 82.3 K and the installed area is 52.8 m2, giving an overall coefficient of 296 W m-2 K-1. The coefficient is the duty divided by the product of the area and the log-mean temperature difference, and it describes the exchanger in the state in which it was assessed: it bundles the wall, the two films, and the fouling present during the run into a single figure. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed. The coefficient therefore carries the fouling accumulated over 90 days and no more. It is not a clean-surface value, and the rate at which fouling builds beyond the assessed period is unmeasured, because the run ended before any cleaning could show what the surface recovers to. A design calculation that enters the assessed coefficient as the clean coefficient imports the fouled state into the new design without stating it, and a comparison against a freshly cleaned unit has to make the same allowance in the opposite direction. The duty and the terminal temperatures stand as measured for the run; the coefficient is the derived quantity, and its scope is the run it was derived from. The preheat duty is also the context for the figure: the exchanger sits in a train in which the hot stream gives up heat it would otherwise lose, and the coefficient is the quantity a later revamp calculation will reach for first, which is why its scope has to travel with it wherever it is quoted.
